 Judgment

Dated this the 13th day of September, 2024 This appeal is filed seeking enhancement of the Award dated 29.04.2017 in O.P.(M.V.) No.549 of 2014 rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Tirur.
The appellant was the petitioner in the said O.P.(M.V.).

Facts in brief:
2.

On 10.06.2013, at about 09.30 P.M., the appellant while travelling as a pillion rider of the motorcycle bearing Registration No.KL- 55/L-8195 driven by his brother (1st respondent) met with an accident at Kodumudi.
Due to the over speeding and sudden application of the brakes, the bike had capsized throwing the appellant off to the road.
As a result, he sustained injuries and was rushed to Nadakkavil Hospital and later to the Moulana Hospital, Perinthalmanna.
He was treated as an inpatient in both the said hospitals and was discharged on 17.06.2013 with advice to continue treatment.

The appellant being a minor during the relevant time, the above O.P.(M.V.) was filed by his father as his next friend, alleging that the accident happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle which was driven by the 1st respondent and owned by the 2nd respondent.
The Insurance Company 2024:KER:69938 was arrayed as the 3rd respondent in the said O.P.(M.V).

Proceedings before the Tribunal:
3. The driver and the owner viz., the 1 st and 2nd respondents in the O.P.(M.V.)
remained ex parte before the Tribunal.
The 3rd respondent Insurance Company filed a written statement admitting the insurance policy of the motorcycle.
The 3rd respondent inter alia contended that the alleged accident was neither reported nor the vehicular documents, including the driving license produced before them for due verification.
Suppression was alleged against the appellant since the facts, that the 1st respondent is the brother of the appellant and that he was being represented by his father, were allegedly not disclosed.

It was further alleged that the claim was Shihab vs Muhammed Abdul Saleem on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105434921/
2 preferred in collusion and hence the 3rd respondent is legally entitled to contest the claim under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 on all grounds.
4. The Tribunal framed four issues and the parties went to trial.
Exts.A1 to A8 and Ext.C1 were marked on the appellant's side.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From the respondents' side no oral or documentary evidence was adduced.

Award of the Tribunal:
5.

The Tribunal, vide Award dated 29.04.2017 held that the 3 rd respondent is liable to pay a total compensation of Rs.5,89,100/- with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation with 2024:KER:69938 proportionate cost as against the claim of Rs.8,00,000/-.
This M.A.C.A. is filed seeking enhancement of the said compensation.
6. Heard Sri.J.R.Prem Navaz, learned counsel appearing for the appellant, and Sri.Suresh Sukumar, learned counsel for the 3rd respondent.

Submissions by the counsel for the appellant:
7. On behalf of the appellant, it is submitted as follows:
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is low and inadequate.
The amount awarded for pain and suffering is inadequate.
Just and fair compensation, taking note of the fact that the appellant may require an attendant for the rest of his life, ought to have been considered by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal erred in not allowing any amounts towards future medical expenses and future loss of earnings taking note of the permanent disability suffered by the appellant.
As a result of the accident, the appellant has been reduced to a vegetative state.
The Tribunal ought to have granted a higher compensation than what was sought as permitted by the Supreme Court [Nagappa v. Gurudayal Singh and others (AIR 2003 SC 674)].

entities.text: Nagappa v. Gurudayal Singh and others (AIR 2003 SC 674)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal ought to have factored in the fluctuations in the cost 2024:KER:69938 of living that could impact the appellant in future.
The Tribunal ought to have taken note of the escalation in the cost of medical treatment for future medical treatment, physiotherapy, nursing etc.

The learned Tribunal ought to have considered the non-pecuniary damages sustained by the appellant,
such as damages for mental and physical shock, pain and suffering, loss of life's amenities and expectations, inconvenience, hardship, discomfort, disappointment,
frustration, and mental stress.
8.
Per contra, the learned counsel for the 3rd respondent Insurance Company submitted that no valid cause or reason to interfere with the Award has been put forth in the appeal.

The compensation awarded by the Tribunal does not call for any Shihab vs Muhammed Abdul Saleem on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105434921/
3 interference and the M.A.C.A. is only to be dismissed.

Discussion and finding:
9.
The injury suffered by the appellant in the accident is borne out from the Wound Certificate (Ext.A4), the discharge certificate from the Moulana Hospital (Ext.A5) and from the Outpatient tickets.
(Ext.A6 series)
. Ext .C1 is the disability certificate issued by the District Medical Board, Govt Hospital, Manjeri.
It is primarily based on these documents that the extent of the injury from the accident and the disability 2024:KER:69938 sustained therefrom is attempted to be proved.

The injuries sustained as discernible from the said documents are as follows:
(a) fracture T 12 vertebra,
(b) lacerated wound over the occipital region,
(c) right brachial plexus injury and post-traumatic compression Ext.C1 certificate records that the appellant has 90% permanent partial disability due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
He was treated as an inpatient in the hospital for 8 days.

10. The approach to be adopted while considering the claim for compensation for injuries suffered by a minor in motor accidents, has been succinctly laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Divya v. National Insurance Co. Ltd. and another (2022 SCC OnLine SC 1488)

entities.text: Divya v. National Insurance Co. Ltd. and another (2022 SCC OnLine SC 1488)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While proceeding to answer the question 'How would you assess the 'just compensation' in such a case when Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, provides for 'just compensation?', the Supreme Court had affirmatively quoted the following observation in Kajal v. Jagdish Chand and others [(2020) 4 SCC 413].

entities.text: Kajal v. Jagdish Chand and others [(2020) 4 SCC 413]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "8. .......You cannot put the plaintiff back again into his original position, but you must bring your reasonable common sense to bear, and you must always recollect that this is the only occasion on which compensation can be given.
The plaintiff can never sue again for it.
You have, therefore, now to give him compensation once and for all.
He has done 2024:KER:69938 no wrong, he has suffered a wrong at the hands of the defendants and you must take care to give him full fair compensation for that which he has suffered."
Bearing in mind the law as laid down above by the Apex Court, I proceed to consider the contentions put forth by the appellant in the case at hand.
11. In the O.P.(M.V.), the compensation sought by the appellant for continuing permanent disability and loss of earning power was Rs.5,60,000/-.

The Tribunal awarded Rs.5,00,000/- following the dictum laid down by the Supreme Court in Mallikarjun v. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited and another (AIR 2014 SC Shihab vs Muhammed Abdul Saleem on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105434921/
4 736).

entities.text: Mallikarjun v. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited and another (AIR 2014 SC Shihab vs Muhammed Abdul Saleem
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal's finding complies with the mandates of law and does not warrant any alteration.
12. Regarding the claim for enhancement of the amounts awarded under the head of pain and suffering, I note that the Tribunal awarded Rs. 20,000/-.

As held by the Supreme Court in Benson George v. Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and another [2022 SCC OnLine SC 238],
the amount of compensation to be awarded under the head pain and suffering, loss of amenities,
and happiness, there cannot be straight jacket formula.

entities.text: Benson George v. Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and another [2022 SCC OnLine SC 238]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Following the above dictum and also considering his age and the nature of injuries, it is 2024:KER:69938 deemed fair to re-fix the amount awarded under the head 'compensation for pain and suffering' to Rs.40,000/-.
13. The appellant had been inpatient for 8 days and had undergone hospitalization and treatment as evident by Ext.A5 and Ext.A6 series.
An amount of Rs.1,500/- had been granted by the Tribunal under the head by stander's expenses and the same amount had been awarded under the head transport to the hospital also.
In the facts and circumstances revealed from the documents, it would be fair, just, and reasonable to increase the same to Rs.10,000/- and 5,000/- respectively.
The appellant had in the O.P.(M.V.) sought an amount of Rs.1,000/- towards extra nourishment.
The Tribunal had granted Rs.500/- under the said head.
I deem it fair to enhance it to Rs.1,000/-.

14. As regards the contentions raised in the M.A.C.A. that the appellant may require an attendant for the rest of his life and that the Tribunal ought to have considered compensation towards future medical expenses and future loss of earnings taking note of the permanent disability suffered by the appellant, no reliable evidence to substantiate the same are seen placed either before the Tribunal or before this court towards substantiating the same.

Similarly, the contention that higher compensation than what was sought could have been granted by the Tribunal as permitted by the Supreme Court in Nagappa's case (supra) 2024:KER:69938 is also not seen to be validly substantiated.
Hence no alteration of the Award of the Tribunal on the said grounds is warranted.

15. In the light of the discussion above, the appeal is disposed of, modifying the compensations granted under the relevant heads of the Award as mentioned below:
 The amount under the head 'pain and suffering' is enhanced from Rs. 20,000/- to Rs.40,000/- .
The amount under the head 'bystanders expense' is re-fixed at Rs.10,000/-.
The amount under the head 'transport to hospital' is enhanced from Rs.1,500/- to Rs.5,000/- and the amount under the head 'extra nourishment' is enhanced to Rs.1,000/-
The amount awarded by the Tribunal under the heading 'compensation for continuing permanent disability and loss of earning power ' is retained.
The Tribunal's assessment of amounts payable under other heads does not call for interference and are hence retained as such.

Conclusion:
